flag.sentence: \section{Discussion and open questions} A score label linked to each trial row preserves the association between a coarse range of assignment probabilities, treatment, and outcome.
flag.fix: \section{Discussion and open questions} A score label linked to each trial row preserves the association between a measurable set of assignment probabilities, treatment, and outcome.

weaknesses: The motivation for the observation scheme is never argued. The introduction asserts that a release attaches a deterministic score label to each row while the full score law is known, but it gives no concrete archive, disclosure-control or privacy rationale explaining why scores are coarsened but their population law is released. Fix: add an introductory paragraph with a concrete release setting, such as a trial archive or registry. Position the problem against disclosure limitation and coarsened-data work, for example interval-data bounds (Manski and Tamer 2002) and statistical-disclosure or differential-privacy release design. Explain why ATE width is the right loss for a data steward.

The paper has no Limitations section, and the restrictive primitives are never weighed. These include exact knowledge of H in the design and known-score sections, a propensity score equal to the stored score under assumption ass:randomized-assignment, outcomes in [0,1], a fixed overlap margin, and a deterministic rather than randomized release. Fix: add a titled Limitations section before Open questions. It should say what fails or is unknown when H is misspecified, when randomized or noisy labels are used, or when ε shrinks with n, since every constant scales as ε^{-1} or ε^{-2}.

The high-resolution result (thm:sharp-high-resolution-constant, lem:paired-high-resolution-quantization) is a weighted-L1 Zador/Bucklew–Wise-type asymptotic. It is positioned only through LemaireMontesPages2020, cited for a density condition. Fix: cite classical high-resolution quantization (Bucklew and Wise 1982; Gersho 1979; Graf and Luschgy 2000). Say plainly that the novelty lies in reducing D_H(g) to a paired weighted absolute-deviation quantization loss. The Zador-type constant itself is not new.

The projection interval in def:external-projection-handle is presented as the attaining procedure without any account of how it is computed or how conservative it is. It is a closed convex hull over an infinite rational sieve, and its Markov-inequality radii 4J/(α√n) and 2J(2−2ε)/(α√m) blow up as 1/α. Fix: after the theorem, state that the construction is an existence device for the rate. Give or sketch a computable version, such as a finite-grid LP over within-cell couplings. Note that the constant C_{ε,J,α,g} is loose. The sharp-constant open question (oeq:external-score-projection) should say what a practical procedure would need.

Several auxiliary data-combination conditions (ass:external-log-iid, ass:external-log-independent) are justified as 'standard' by citing MarellaPfeffermann2019, which concerns informative sampling in statistical matching and is a weak authority for i.i.d. two-sample sampling. Fix: either drop the citation and motivate the conditions directly, for example that the score log comes from a separate operational period, or cite a data-combination source that actually adopts two independent i.i.d. samples. Also discuss when the log and the trial share the same score law H.

The fixed-law interval (lem:fixed-released-law-baseline) is proved in full in the appendix, yet the verification scope says it is 'used as a cited input' from FanShermanShum2014. The reader cannot tell which part is original and which is imported. Fix: in the introduction and the verification subsection, state exactly which statement is taken from Fan–Sherman–Shum, with the locator. Present the appendix proof as an adaptation to labelled cells and atoms. Separate that from the Lean-verified content.
defects: The section 'Designing a finite-label release' opens with 'The cellwise criterion in \cref{obj:thm:universal-point-identification}'. The cellwise expression is in thm:all-label-ambiguity; change the reference to \cref{obj:thm:all-label-ambiguity}.

def:mean-endpoints uses Q_F before synth_4 (generalized quantile) is defined, and the text 'The generalized quantile Q_F in \cref{obj:synth_4}' is a forward reference. Move synth_4 ahead of def:mean-endpoints.
θ(P) is defined twice: once in the section 3 prose ('\theta(P)=\mathbb E_P(Y_1-Y_0)') and again as synth_1 in section 6. Delete synth_1, or move it to section 3 and drop the prose definition.

synth_1 contains garbled text: 'For any measure P on full rows ... with score parameter ε and J labels'. P should be a probability law, and 'score parameter ε and J labels' asserts nothing. Rewrite as 'For a law P in \mathfrak P(H,g), \theta(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y_1-Y_0]'.
synth_2 (Treatment-arm set 𝒜={0,1}) and synth_3 (Released-label alphabets) are trivial standalone definitions. Merge them into one notation paragraph, or fold them into def:arm-cell-primitives.

C_r, p_a, q_ar, E_ar, W_ar and the endpoints \underline\mu_a, \overline\mu_a are defined in def:arm-cell-primitives and def:mean-endpoints, then redefined verbatim inside thm:all-label-ambiguity, thm:universal-point-identification and lem:fixed-released-law-baseline. Replace the restatements with \cref{obj:def:arm-cell-primitives,obj:def:mean-endpoints}.

def:high-resolution-handle ('High-resolution handle H_opt') uses formalization jargon ('handle'). The object is vacuous and never used afterwards. Delete it and describe the two-step argument in prose.

The paper uses 'certificate' jargon in several places: 'lower certificates', 'trial certificate', 'score-log certificate' (text after thm:external-score-root-order), 'the positive trial certificate', 'this eventual certificate' and 'both displayed certificate coefficients' (in proofs). Replace these with 'lower bound' and 'lower-bound constant'.

'totalized interval' and 'For other values of ε, set D_{ε,J}=∅' in def:external-projection-handle are Lean totalization artifacts. Say that the interval is set to {0} when the retained set is empty, and drop the ε-case clause, since ass:overlap is maintained.

def:external-projection-handle says 'the weights are viewed as nonnegative extended-real numbers' and 'defined for ... a real number α'. These are formalization residue. State that α∈(0,1/2) and that the weights are nonnegative reals.

'rank contacts' ('quantile distributions with rank contacts' in the introduction; 'transport quantiles with rank contacts' after thm:external-score-root-order) is undefined. Define it, or replace it with 'quantile functions with flat pieces or atoms'.

In def:external-projection-handle, 'I(b) be the interval given by its two quantile-transport average treatment effect endpoints' has no formal definition in the main text. The endpoint maps Ψ_a^± are defined only inside the appendix proof of thm:external-score-root-order, so the central procedure is incomplete in the body. Define Ψ_a^± and I(b) in the algorithm environment.
The symbol J_{n,m} in def:external-projection-handle clashes with the label count J and with the honest classes 𝒥_{n,K,α} and 𝒥^{ext}. Rename it, for example \widehat I_{n,m}.

len, length and |C_n| are all used for interval length ('\operatorname{len}', '\operatorname{length}(C_{n,m})', '|C_n(x)|') without a definition. Define len once in the notation paragraph and use it consistently.
The notation 𝒫(𝓔) in def:score-lower-density-class and def:external-law-class ('H\in\mathcal P(\mathcal E)') is never defined. Add 'the set of Borel probability laws on 𝓔' to the notation paragraph.
thm:sharp-high-resolution-constant uses g_K:𝓔→{0,…,K−1}, while 𝒢_K and ℛ_K use {1,…,K}. Re-index to {1,…,K} so that g_K∈𝒢_K is literal.

The proof of thm:sharp-high-resolution-constant says 'At K=0, assign zero to the two auxiliary scaled quantities; both bounds then read 0≤0≤0'. This is a formalization artifact, and the theorem concerns positive K. Delete it.
The proof of thm:all-label-ambiguity ends with 'The hypotheses also cover the index-set boundary: 𝓔 contains ε, so the value g(ε) ensures ℛ_J is nonempty'. The clause is vacuous; delete it.
lem:released-arm-cell-masses states 'Let H be a measure ... Then H and P_rel are probability laws', which is a formalization artifact. State H as a probability law and drop the conclusion.

In lem:fixed-released-law-baseline, '(Overlap.) The score support satisfies \cref{obj:ass:overlap}' is inaccurate, because ass:overlap constrains ε, not the support. Write 'The overlap parameter satisfies \cref{obj:ass:overlap}'.

In thm:external-score-root-order, the '(Joint sampling.)' hypothesis restates def:external-experiment, which already defines 𝕈 as a product law. Drop the hypothesis, or cite \cref{obj:def:external-experiment}.

thm:external-score-root-order says the procedure 'agrees pointwise as a closed interval with the projection interval'. This is verification phrasing. State that the projection interval C_{n,m} of \cref{obj:def:external-projection-handle} belongs to the honest class.
def:honest-procedures writes P^{⊗n}[θ(P)∈C_n((R_i,A_i,Y_i))], whereas later text uses P_rel^{⊗n}. Use \mathcal L_P(R,A,Y)^{\otimes n} consistently.

ass:density-lower does not require m_f>0, but the following prose says 'when the floor is positive', and thm:k-label-rate adds '(Density floor.) m_f>0'. State m_f>0 in the assumption or in the class definition once.

def:score-lower-density-class opens with 'Under \cref{obj:ass:density-lower}, the class of score laws is', which is circular because the class itself imposes the density floor. Remove the 'Under ...' clause.

The constant C_{ε,J,α,g} in thm:external-score-root-order does not depend on g beyond J, according to its explicit formula in the proof. Drop the subscript g, or note that the dependence is only through J.

The verification-scope subsection says 'The theorem statements and formal proofs are machine-checked in Lean 4'. It omits the toolchain, commit and per-statement mapping promised in the author footnote. Add these details or amend the footnote.

weaknesses: Claims versus assumptions: The main claims generally retain their formal conditions, but the introduction should state more prominently that the sharp high-resolution constant requires a continuous, strictly positive density and that the joint external-log rate is established at a positive limiting trial-to-log ratio.

Positioning: The related-work section lists several literatures without explaining precisely which result is inherited and which release-design question is new. Add a short comparison centered on the fixed-law result attributed to Fan, Sherman, and Shum and the paper’s subsequent optimization over labels and released laws.

Assumption discussion: The setup motivates overlap and the density floor as technical aids but gives little account of their substantive restrictiveness. Explain what a known population score law, deterministic score labels, and a common positive density floor require of an actual release.

Inference framing: The two inference sections optimize different risks—total interval length with a known score law and positive excess length with an independent log. Explain why each criterion answers its stated decision problem, especially why the latter includes trial-sampling variation as well as score-law learning.

Writing: The main narrative is interrupted by long definitions and a detailed rational-sieve algorithm. Introduce the projection interval through its empirical measures and purpose in the main text, then move its implementation details to the appendix.
defects: “whose local value is proportional to the square root of the score density divided by the product” is ambiguous about the scope of the square root. Write the weight explicitly as \(\sqrt{f(e)/[e(1-e)]}\).

The mean-endpoint definition uses \(Q_{F_{ar}}\) and \(Q_{W_{ar}}\) before the generalized-quantile definition, then points forward to \cref{obj:synth_4}. Move the generalized-quantile definition before the endpoint formulas.

The ATE functional \(\theta(P)\) is stated in the setup but formally defined only in the later known-score inference section. Move \cref{obj:synth_1} to the setup and combine it with the initial definition.

The high-resolution theorem defines \(g_K:\mathcal E\to\{0,\ldots,K-1\}\), while the release class defining \(\Delta_K(H)\) uses \(\{1,\ldots,K\}\). Use one label convention or state the relabeling explicitly.

“High-resolution handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{opt}}\)” describes an “uncrossing or intervalization result” without stating a usable result, and the proof does not invoke it. Delete this placeholder definition or replace it with a precise lemma that is used.

“score distributions with rank contacts” appears in the introduction and external-log discussion without an explanation. Define the term or replace it with a concrete description of the quantile configurations covered.

The projection algorithm says rational weights are “viewed as nonnegative extended-real numbers,” although clipping rational weights yields finite nonnegative values. Say “finite nonnegative weights.”
“For other values of \(\varepsilon\), set \(\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}=\varnothing\)” is dead text under the paper’s standing overlap condition. Remove it from the reader-facing algorithm.

The external-log theorem says the procedure “agrees pointwise as a closed interval with the projection interval,” which adds no usable property to the preceding construction. State directly that the projection interval attains the bound.
“At \(K=0\), assign zero to the two auxiliary scaled quantities” in the high-resolution proof addresses a value outside the theorem’s positive-integer domain. Delete the sentence.
The density-floor class is introduced for arbitrary \(m_f>0\), although it is empty when \(m_f(1-2\varepsilon)>1\). State the feasible range when presenting uniform comparisons over that class.

The appendix calls the lower-bound arguments “certificates” and the main text calls the high-resolution ingredient a “handle.” Replace these formalization-flavored terms with “lower bounds” and a precise mathematical lemma or construction.

weaknesses: Motivation for the observation scheme is thin. The introduction does not name a setting where a trial archive releases a deterministic score label and the exact population score law H is also known: who holds H, why the row-level score is withheld, and why the release is deterministic rather than noisy. Add a paragraph early in the introduction with one or two concrete settings (for example a platform experiment with stratified propensity bins, or a public-use trial file with coarsened assignment strata). State plainly that exact knowledge of H is a strong idealization, and point to the score-log section as the relaxation.

The design criterion D_H(g) is a supremum over all released outcome laws, and \cref{obj:thm:all-label-ambiguity} shows that Bernoulli(1/2) outcomes attain it. The paper presents this as the natural measure of information retained, but never discusses how conservative it is for a given data set: the realized sharp width at the actual P_rel can be far smaller. In the discussion after \cref{obj:thm:all-label-ambiguity}, or in the Discussion section, explain that D_H(g) is an outcome-free design guarantee. Contrast it with the fixed-law width of \cref{obj:lem:fixed-released-law-baseline}, which an analyst reports once data are released.

The external-score projection interval (\cref{obj:def:external-projection-handle}) is a sieve over arbitrary finite lists of rational atoms, so it is defined for existence rather than computation. Its constant C_{ε,J,α,g} grows linearly in J, α^{-1} and ε^{-2}, and it gives no K-rate. The text presents it as 'the interval used in the rate result' and gives no account of practical implementation or of how conservative the Markov-based radii are. Add a limitations paragraph saying that the construction establishes the rate, and name a computable relaxation (for example a finite-grid linear program) as future work. Also comment on how the upper-bound constant depends on J, so readers can see how it interacts with the K^{-1} design analysis.

Assumption discussion is largely boilerplate citation: each assumption gets 'standard ... \citep{FanShermanShum2014}' or '\citep{MarellaPfeffermann2019}'. Three restrictions are never discussed. (i) Bounded outcomes in [0,1]: what rescaling it implies and how widths scale with the outcome range. (ii) The fixed overlap margin ε: every constant blows up as ε→0, which matters for designs with extreme propensities. (iii) iid superpopulation sampling for a trial whose assignment is Bernoulli by design. Replace the generic citations with a sentence on the restrictiveness of each assumption.

Positioning omits the most closely related literatures. There is no quantization literature (e.g. Graf and Luschgy) for \cref{obj:thm:sharp-high-resolution-constant}, whose constant and companding rule are classical in form. There is no coarsened or interval-covariate partial identification (e.g. Manski and Tamer 2002). There is no statistical disclosure control or data-release literature, even though the paper speaks of 'disclosure'. Add these to the related-work section and state precisely what is new relative to standard high-resolution quantization: the paired reciprocal-weight loss and the intervalization step.

The link between the known-score minimax result and the design result should be argued more carefully. The K^{-1} lower bound in \cref{obj:thm:minimax-honest-length} comes entirely from worst-case ambiguity over the causal class, so the recommendation K ∝ √n is a worst-case tuning rule. State this in the paragraph after the theorem, and note that for favourable outcome laws a coarser release may lose nothing.
defects: Introduction, paragraph 3: the text is mangled: 'cumulative weight  sqrt{f(e)/[e(1-e)]}, where  (f(e) ) is the score density at score  (e"];.' Replace it with '$\int_\varepsilon^{e}\sqrt{f(t)/[t(1-t)]}\,dt$, where $f$ is the score density'.

\cref{obj:synth_4} (generalized quantile) is used in \cref{obj:def:mean-endpoints} and in the sentence after it, but it is defined only after \cref{obj:def:sharp-ate-set}. Move the generalized-quantile definition before the mean-endpoint definition.

The released-label alphabet (\cref{obj:synth_3}) and the treatment-arm set (\cref{obj:synth_2}) are trivial standalone definitions. Merge them into one notation sentence or definition, and fold \cref{obj:def:k-label-releases} into it.

\cref{obj:def:high-resolution-handle} ('High-resolution handle $\mathsf H_{\mathrm{opt}}$') is formalization jargon, asserts nothing mathematical, and is never used afterwards. Delete it and describe the proof strategy in prose.

Add a short discussion of plausible release and score-log settings and the role of each restriction.
